route.name: Beirut-Damascus Railway
route.notes: The rack section over Mount Lebanon (Dar al-Baidar pass) is the defining feature.  [gauge_mm] DISCREPANCY: sources give 1,050 mm narrow gauge with an Abt rack section (opened 3 Aug 1895). The project system lists 1,435 mm — likely an error.  [countries] COUNTRY CORRECTIONS vs the project list: Yahfoufa is in LEBANON (as listed), but every station beyond it — Serghaya, Ain Hur, Zabadani, Madaya, El-Tekkieh, Souk Wadi Barada, Deir Qanoun, Ain el Fijeh, Achrafieh, Jdeideh, Al-Hama, Dummar and Damascus — is in SYRIA. The project list mislabels these Barada-gorge stations as Lebanon. 'Souk/Suk Wadi Barada' was also DUPLICATED in the list (once Lebanon, once Syria) — merged into one Syrian station.  [route] Ordered station chain + altitudes from the Beirut-Damascus Railway project site.
route.history: Opened to Beirut on 3 August 1895 at 1,050 mm gauge. From the coast the line climbed Mount Lebanon on Abt RACK sections to the summit at Dahr al-Baidar (~1,490 m, ~37 km from Beirut), descended to the Beqaa plain at Chtaura, and reached the junction at Rayak. From Rayak the Damascus branch climbed again to a summit around Serghaya/Ain Hur (~1,380 m) before descending the Barada gorge through Zabadani and Ain el Fijeh to Damascus (~700 m). The full trip initially took about 9 hours and terminated at Baramke, Qanawat and Midan stations in Damascus.
